text:
ConocoPhillips fell 3.6% today as oil prices dropped sharply, with US crude sliding to $89.53 per barrel from above $140 just days ago. The timing coincides with escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iran attacking US positions in Kuwait and the Strait of Hormuz facing sustained disruptions—which typically support oil prices by signaling supply risk. The fact that prices are falling anyway suggests markets are pricing in either a near-term ceasefire, reduced demand concerns, or simply a pullback after the sharp run-up earlier this week.

The broader context matters: even with the Strait of Hormuz unreliable and regional conflicts mounting, the market appears skeptical that these tensions will sustain the supply premium that drove oil higher recently. For a major oil producer, that shift in market sentiment—not the geopolitical facts on the ground—is what moves the stock.
